_doc: LATEX MATH NOTATION -> meaning/operator-tree (graph data, the agent's grammar). LaTeX math is a NOTATION SYSTEM; notation is LEARNABLE the SAME way as the agent's other notations (notation-is-learnable). This seed MIRRORS seeds/math_prose_constructions.json: the LaTeX constructions PARSE into the SAME operator-tree the prose grammar composes (op(args) nested, bottoming at HELD atoms). The agent READS a LaTeX string -> the operator-tree via these constructions + comprehend_structure's recursion. Where the operation is HELD (\partial -> boundary_operator ∂, acquired in acquire_boundary_operator) it grounds/computes; where un-held (\ker / \im / quotient) it is the NAMED acquirable residual already named in math_prose_constructions. These are the CORE math constructions (super/subscript, frac, named operators, homology/cohomology, blackboard/Greek, set-builder) — CONSTRUCTIONS (general), NOT per-formula rules. Coverage grows by adding entries (graph data, not code). The HONEST residual = the LaTeX LONG TAIL (every macro/package/\newcommand) + the un-held operations (kernel/image), each acquirable by READING the next instance.
_doc_macros: NAMED-OPERATOR macros: a LaTeX control sequence -> the operator/atom name the prose grammar holds. `held`/`held_runnable` mirror math_prose_constructions: ∂ (boundary_operator) is HELD (the recursion bottoms out at it); kernel/image/quotient are UN-HELD (the acquirable residual). `arity` says how many bracketed/space-delimited arguments the macro consumes (prefix operators). The op/atom NAME is the SAME token the prose constructions use, so a LaTeX-parsed tree and a prose-parsed tree are the SAME structure.

operator_macros.name: boundary_operator
operator_macros._doc: ∂ — the boundary operator, HELD (acquire_boundary_operator, ∂∂=0). A subscripted ∂_n is the boundary operator in degree n; the recursion bottoms out here.

operator_macros.name: kernel
operator_macros._doc: \ker X -> kernel(X): inputs the map X sends to zero. Un-held (acquirable by reading its meta-def — same residual as math_prose_constructions kernel_of).

operator_macros.name: image
operator_macros._doc: \operatorname{im} X -> image(X): outputs of the map X. Un-held.

operator_macros.name: rank
operator_macros._doc: \rank X / \rank(X) -> rank(X): the GENERAL unary-function construction (a named operator macro applied to its recursively-parsed argument), the SAME as \dim/\deg. Un-held LEAF unless a held rank tool is bound (parse-general; eval depends on the held leaf).

operator_macros.name: torsion
operator_macros._doc: \torsion H_k -> torsion(H_k): the order of the TORSION subgroup of the integral homology in degree k (|torsion H_k|). The SAME GENERAL unary-function construction as \dim/\rank. Held LEAF when a torsion tool is bound (the SNF-over-Z invariant-factor product, reason._smith_normal_form_factors); |torsion H_1(RP^2)| = |Z/2| = 2.

_doc_structure: STRUCTURE macros: LaTeX that builds an operator-tree NODE from its arguments (a fraction, a sub/superscript application, a quotient). The OP name again MIRRORS the prose grammar (\frac and the '/' quotient both map to `modulo` — A/B as a quotient group, the un-held operation the homology formula needs).

structure_macros._doc: \frac{A}{B} -> div(A, B): the GENERAL fraction construction (any \frac of two recursively-parsed operands). `braced` says the macro takes its two args as separate { } groups (the tokenizer no longer slurps the first brace). Held-runnable: the DSL Div Term computes A/B (the SET/GROUP quotient ker/im is written with the infix '/', which still maps to the un-held `modulo`).

\binom{n}{k} -> binomial(n, k): the GENERAL binomial-coefficient construction (n choose k). `braced` two-arg. UN-HELD: there is no held binomial LEAF/Term yet (the named residual) — the construction PARSES general but the eval STALLS until a binomial tool is held (honest: parse-general, un-held-leaf).
the infix '/' between two operator-tree operands is the QUOTIENT (ker ∂_n / im ∂_{n+1}) — the same `modulo` op.

the infix '+' is ADDITION between two operands (a + b). A GENERAL arithmetic operator (NOT per-formula) — the SAME construction parses any sum-of-terms (b_0 + b_2, a_1 + a_2). Held-runnable: the DSL Plus Term computes it.

the infix '-' is SUBTRACTION/DIFFERENCE between two operands (a - b). A GENERAL arithmetic operator (NOT per-formula); chains left-associatively with '+' so b_0 - b_1 + b_2 - b_3 reads as ((b_0 - b_1) + b_2) - b_3. Held-runnable: the DSL Minus Term computes it.

the infix '*' is MULTIPLICATION between two operands (a * b). A GENERAL arithmetic operator (NOT per-formula); binds tighter than +/- so (-1)^k * b_k groups as a product. Held-runnable: the DSL Times Term computes it.

x \cup y -> cup_product(x, y): the cup product on cohomology classes (Alexander-Whitney, reason._cup_product). The GENERAL binary cohomology-product construction (any x, y), keyed on the \cup SYNTAX. UN-HELD as a SCALAR LEAF: the held cup product takes COCHAIN VECTORS (p,q,alpha,beta), not two scalar leaves, so the construction PARSES general but the scalar eval STALLS (the named residual — held as a cochain op, not a scalar-binary leaf).
x \smile y -> cup_product(x, y): the \smile spelling of the cup product. Same op as \cup.
A \cong B -> isomorphic(A, B): A is isomorphic to B.
A \to B -> map(A, B): a morphism from A to B.

_doc_indexed: SUB/SUPERSCRIPT: `X_{...}` (subscript = index/degree) and `X^{...}` (superscript = degree/power). On a named operator ∂_n the subscript is the DEGREE (∂ in degree n); on a homology head H_n / H^n it selects homology/cohomology of that degree. The parse keeps the index as an `index` on the node so ∂_n and ∂_{n+1} are DISTINGUISHED (the homology formula needs both).
_doc_arg_slots: ARG SLOTS — a head's parenthesised argument is a COMPOUND OBJECT with a TYPED ARGUMENT STRUCTURE, not a single expression. `arg_slots` NAMES the roles a comma/semicolon-separated argument list fills, in order. H^n(G, M) and H^n(X; A) are two-argument functors: the FIRST slot is the SPACE/GROUP the (co)homology is OF, the SECOND is the COEFFICIENT module/ring. A bare H_n(X) fills only the first slot (default Z coefficients). The reader splits the top-level (depth-0) commas (and the LaTeX `;` coefficient separator) into one arg per slot, typed by role, INSTEAD of collapsing them into a `times` product. This is the GENERAL typing of any homological-functor compound object (group cohomology H^n(G,M), Ext^n(A,B), Tor_n(A,B)), graph-data-driven (the slots are seed DATA, not a per-formula rule). With one argument the extra slots are absent (honest partial typing).

indexed_heads.name: homology
indexed_heads._doc: H_n(X) -> homology(X) in degree n (subscript). H_n(X; A) -> homology of X with coefficients A. math_prose_constructions has the homology STRUCTURE the agent already COMPUTES in compute_homology.

indexed_heads.name: cohomology
indexed_heads._doc: H^n(X) -> cohomology(X) in degree n (superscript). H^n(G, M) -> GROUP cohomology of G with coefficients in the module M (the first slot is the group/space, the second the coefficient module) — typed as a two-argument functor, NOT a product of G and M.

indexed_heads.name: bordism
indexed_heads._doc: \Omega^{Spin}_n -> Spin bordism in degree n (the HLE-tier rung — un-held, named in compute_homology's not-reached rungs).

indexed_heads.name: ext
indexed_heads._doc: \mathrm{Ext}^n(A, B) -> the n-th Ext functor of the pair (A, B): a TWO-ARGUMENT homological functor (the SAME compound-object typing as H^n(G,M)), keyed on the head + the comma-separated argument list. Un-held.

indexed_heads.name: tor
indexed_heads._doc: \mathrm{Tor}_n(A, B) -> the n-th Tor functor of (A, B): a TWO-ARGUMENT homological functor. Un-held.

_doc_quantifier: QUANTIFIER / big-operator macros: \sum / \prod / \int with sub/superscript bounds; \bigoplus / \bigotimes / \bigcup / \bigcap. They map to the aggregator op name; the bound (subscript) + limit (superscript) are kept as args.

quantifier_macros._doc: \sum_{k} <body> -> the SUM fold binding k over the family, the recursively-parsed body the summand. GENERAL big-operator (any binder/range/body). Held-runnable: the DSL Sum fold Term computes it (cmsg165-167).

\prod_{k} <body> -> the PRODUCT fold binding k over the family, the recursively-parsed body the factor. GENERAL big-operator (the SAME binder construction as \sum, op=product). Held-runnable: the DSL Prod fold Term computes it.

\min_{k} <body> -> the MIN-over-family fold binding k, the recursively-parsed body the quantity minimised. GENERAL operator-over-a-family (ground_definition/order_n's held Fold). Held-runnable: the DSL MinOver fold Term.
\max_{k} <body> -> the MAX-over-family fold binding k. GENERAL operator-over-a-family. Held-runnable: the DSL MaxOver fold Term.
\sup_{k} <body> -> the supremum, a MAX-over-family fold (the held finite-family realisation). Held-runnable: MaxOver.
\inf_{k} <body> -> the infimum, a MIN-over-family fold. Held-runnable: MinOver.

_doc_relations: RELATION / SET macros: membership and inclusion. They render to a readable WORD so the genus-differentia prose grammar reads them (\in -> 'in', \subseteq -> 'a subset of') — the symbol-carried definition survives into comprehension.

relation_macros._doc: K \trianglelefteq G -> 'K normal in G': K is a normal subgroup of G. An aside predication on the subject (the asked invariant is the rank, not the normal-subgroup relation); the held reader renders it to a readable relation word the comprehension window excises as a clause aside.

_doc_named_symbols: NAMED-OPERATOR SYMBOL renderings: a notation symbol (a function-named operator or a standard named map) -> the readable PROSE NAME the prose grammar's atoms/operators cover, so the SAME held LaTeX reader that reads every formula resolves the symbolic shorthand structurally — NOT a bespoke re.sub in a calling module. Each is graph DATA the reader consumes (the agent extends its held reader by adding an entry). `\operatorname{Ker}` / `Ker` (the capitalised function-name spelling of the kernel) -> 'kernel' (the SAME word \ker / \operatorname{ker} render to). `h_*` / `h_{*}` (the standard symbol for the Hurewicz homomorphism h_*: pi_1 -> H_1) -> 'the hurewicz map' (the SAME atom the prose 'the hurewicz map' types to). The render is longest-symbol-first; these run BEFORE the generic font-wrapper unwrap (which would otherwise strip \operatorname{Ker} to the bare token 'Ker').
_doc_symbol_render: SYMBOL RENDERING: macros that render to a SHORT readable token so the LaTeX-bearing prose SURVIVES the strip into comprehension (instead of being DROPPED to nothing). \mathbb{Z} -> 'Z' (the integers), Greek \alpha -> 'alpha', \mathcal{C} -> 'C'. The point: '$M$ is finite if $M$ is finite as an $R$-module' renders to 'M is finite if M is finite as an R-module' — the subject SURVIVES (vs the lossy strip 'finite if is finite as an -module').
_doc_greek: Greek macros -> their name (a readable token). Used both for rendering ($\alpha$ -> 'alpha') and as indexed-head/atom names where applicable.
_doc_wrappers: FONT / GROUPING wrappers rendered to their bare content (the term survives): \mathcal{C} -> 'C', \mathrm{Spin} -> 'Spin', \text{...} -> the text, \operatorname{Spec} -> 'Spec'. The argument's content is what carries meaning.
_doc_setbuilder: SET-BUILDER: \{ x \mid P(x) \} / \{ x : P(x) \} -> the set of x such that P(x). Rendered to readable prose ('the set of x such that ...') so the genus grammar can read a set-builder-defined object.
